title: The Future of Work: Toran Bruce Richards, Silen Naihin et al
talk_summary: This is largely an AutoGPT community/roadmap keynote (stars, contributors, funding) with little technical mechanism. The only transferable ideas are using a benchmark as a 'compass' in CI to measure agent improvement, and treating code as the fundamental agent capability.

takeaways.what_they_do: They built a benchmark to quantitatively direct development of the open-source agent and run it in their CI pipeline on a schedule, so they can tell whether changes improve or regress agent success rates across categories.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we created a benchmark to direct the development of the open source repo and quantitatively know if we were improving
takeaways.numbers: success rate trend 35% to 55% over August; described as 'very noisy, very messy'

takeaways.technique: Benchmark the reviewer, not just the code
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat 'is this PR good?' as an unmeasurable question until they define a benchmark; the same logic applies to an LLM PR reviewer whose recall is unknown.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we had no way to know whether the poll requests were good and how do we even test these pull requests

takeaways.technique: Treat agent over-permissioning as a first-class failure mode
takeaways.what_they_do: They flag 'innocently malicious' agent errors (an agent asked to delete JSON files in one directory deleted all JSON on the laptop) and prompt injection from visited pages as blockers to commercial viability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent ended up deleting all the Json files on a laptop

takeaways.technique: Code as the universal agent substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue coding agents are the fundamental agents because code is the digital fabric, so a coding-capable agent can accomplish most digital work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code is King we've realized that coding agents are the fundamental agents
